title: PRD: cache regeneration runbook + progressive traffic shepherding
creator: Avery Chen
description: Background: Following the 2026-03-02 KV cache regen incident (incident-2026-03-kv-regen) the postmortem called out two recurring gaps: lack of a deterministic runbook for cache regeneration with memory-pressure signals, and missing progressive traffic steering (canary + shepherding) during kernel/quantization rollouts. This PRD formalizes the postmortem actions into product requirements, scope boundaries, and acceptance criteria. Goals: 1) Define an operator-facing runbook that triggers deterministic KV-cache regen and safe cache rebuilds without causing mass cold-starts. 2) Add traffic shepherding primitives to the runtime routing policy for progressive rollouts and automated rollback gates. 3) Provide verification suites and synthetic checks to ensure regressions are detectable pre- and post-deploy. Out of scope: low-level kernel changes (ENG-owned), long-term model-level quantization strategy (Research-owned). Scope changes from previous PRD draft: - Added a new 'shepherding' policy type to routing (previously only canary and global). - Require automatic synthetic verification post-regeneration (added per postmortem ask). Stakeholders: PM: Avery Chen; Eng leads: Lucas Nguyen (runtime), Priya Rai (orchestration); SRE: Marco Silva; Design: Elena Ortiz. Key user stories: - As an oncall, I need a one-click KV-cache regen runbook with clear prechecks and rollback steps. - As a release engineer, I need progressive traffic shepherding so I can ramp new kernels to 5/20/50/100% with automated SLO checks. Success metrics: - Mean time to recover from KV-cache regen incidents decreases by 40% within first 3 months. - No more than 2% increases in P99 latency during regen rollouts. - Automated canary verification catches regressions in >95% of synthetic runs.
acceptance_criteria: Operator runbook doc published in Confluence with prechecks, exact commands, expected metrics, and rollback steps.
Automated runbook implementation that runs regen with prechecks (memory, disk, KV size) and can be executed from Console/runbook API.
Traffic shepherding policy added to runtime routing: supports fractional ramps (5/20/50/100), health gates based on per-route SLOs and token-error-rate.
Canary verification job produces pass/fail signal to routing layer within 5 minutes of canary start.
E2E verification harness (synthetic prompts) added to CI that simulates regen and ramp and asserts latency and token-accuracy thresholds.
Dashboard with regen metrics and canary rollouts added to Console; alert rules configured for SLO degradation during ramp.
Rollback automation triggers within 2 minutes of a failing canary and returns traffic to last-known-good variant.
verification_plan: Runbook dry-run executed on staging with intentionally induced memory-pressure; document timings and side-effects.
Synthetic canary runs using three worst-case prompt sets from postmortem; verify detection of quality regressions.
Chaos test: run regen while increasing traffic; assert no cascading cold starts beyond defined threshold.
Oncall playthrough with SRE and Runtime leads to validate operator steps and time-to-completion.
Release cut with shepherding enabled on a small customer cohort; monitor for 48 hours before ramping.
